note: Literature establishes BRD4 mutations as causing a milder or atypical/non-classic CdLS phenotype with less severe limb and cognitive involvement.

evidence.text: BRD4 pathogenic variants are recognized as causing non-classic or milder forms of Cornelia de Lange syndrome compared to classic NIPBL-related presentations.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 Gene Alterations: A Literature Review
source.quote: variations in several other genes, including BRD4, have been identified as causative factors for non-classic or milder forms of the syndrome.

evidence.text: An international cohort study of 14 new patients with BRD4 alterations delineated the clinical dysmorphisms and phenotypic spectrum across ages, noting a distinct cohesinopathy pattern.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We report the first cohort of patients with BRD4-related disorder and delineate the dysmorphic features at different ages. This work extends the phenotypic spectrum of cohesinopathies and characterize a new clinically relevant and recognizable pattern, distinguishable from the other cohesinopathies.
